name: Elder Mosswick
description: A lean man in his sixties, or so he appears. His hair is white as chalk, his eyes a pale, unsettling green. He walks without a cane but moves too smoothly for his age. He is the last person in Thornwick who remembers what the founding charter actually said — because he was there when it was signed. He is far older than anyone knows.
attitude: Wary ally — will help the players but withholds the truth about himself until cornered
relation_niveau: Neutral at first meeting; potential ally if players earn his trust

voix.registre: Careful, old-fashioned, deliberately plain. Uses the vocabulary of a village elder, never that of a scholar — he has spent a century hiding how much he knows.
voix.rythme: Long sentences that arrive somewhere other than where they started. He answers the question next to the one he was asked.
voix.sous_tension: Goes quiet and asks a question back. Under real pressure his sentences shorten and the old cadence surfaces — a way of speaking nobody in Thornwick has used for eighty years.
lexique: Charters, names, signatures, what is written and what is owed — his images all come from binding agreements
Speaks of the village as a household: doors, hearths, thresholds
tics: Calls people 'child' regardless of their age
Says 'as it happens' before a piece of information he has in fact prepared
ne_dit_jamais: Never says 'fae' or 'the Court' — says 'them', 'the other side', 'our neighbours'
Never says 'I remember' about anything older than forty years, even when he does

established_facts: Is the last active Warden and holds the cold-iron bell
Knows the Veil is fae-caused and connected to the founding charter
Has begun sending people out of Thornwick to warn newcomers
Claims the charter was signed 'long before his time' — this is a lie
connaissances_privees: Knows the bell only works three more times — he has counted, and he has told no one
Knows the name of the villager who let the mist in eighty years ago; it was his brother
Knows exactly what the charter demands, having watched it signed — and knows the players will ask him to read it aloud eventually
gm_hypotheses: He is the third soul the Pale Court seeks — the charter bears his true name, not his current one
He has been extending his life through small, private bargains with the Court for decades — he owes more than he admits
If the players discover his secret, he may either confess and help destroy the charter, or flee and doom the village
inventory: Cold-Iron Bell (taken from the Hall rack)
A folded note with names of villagers he suspects are mist-shades
A small vial of chalk-water (old ritual use, purpose unclear)

lignes_rouges: Will not willingly reveal his true age or the extent of his own bargains
Will not leave Thornwick while villagers remain in danger — his guilt keeps him there
peurs: Fears that destroying the charter means his own life ends — he suspects his longevity is tied to the Court's debt
motivations_personnelles: Wants to see Thornwick safe even at personal cost — guilt has accumulated for a century
Hopes the players will find a loophole he has been unable to see, being too close to the problem

history.reason: The Veil took two more villagers — the Court is close to its count
The newcomers agreed to help Thornwick without demanding payment

name: The Lady of Sighs
premiere_rencontre: Not yet encountered — heard only as a voice in the Mire
description: Tall, pale, dressed in layered grey silk that moves without wind. Her face is too symmetrical. She speaks in a measured, unhurried tone as though every word is being inscribed somewhere. She is neither cruel nor kind — she is contractual. A bargain is a bargain. She will honour hers to the letter and expect the same.
attitude: Neutral — bound by her own laws as much as anyone else
relation_niveau: Antagonist by circumstance; potential negotiating partner if approached correctly

voix.registre: Court formality, absolute precision. Addresses everyone by title or by what they have done, never by an assumed name. Contractions do not exist in her mouth.
voix.rythme: Even, unhurried, each clause complete. She never interrupts and never repeats herself — repetition would imply the first statement was insufficient.
voix.sous_tension: Becomes shorter and more exact, and starts naming prices unprompted. Her courtesy does not slip; it narrows.
lexique: Debts, terms, tallies, what was promised and what remains outstanding
Speaks of people as parties to an agreement, of deaths as settlements
tics: Restates an offer in exact terms before accepting it, as if reading it aloud for a witness
ne_dit_jamais: Never says 'please', never threatens — she states consequences as scheduled facts
Never lies outright: she is bound by her own laws. She omits, and lets an incomplete truth do the work

established_facts: Is the voice and authority of the Pale Court in the mortal world
Seeks three souls to complete the century-old debt — has two; needs one more
Cannot enter a chalk circle drawn with iron filings
Will accept a counter-bargain if its weight is equal
connaissances_privees: Knows the charter carries a flaw her own Court has never been able to exploit, and has never been asked about it
Knows Elder Mosswick's true name, and that speaking it aloud would settle his debt on the spot
gm_hypotheses: She is genuinely bound by fae law and cannot take what was not offered — the players can use this
She finds humans interesting in the way a collector finds rare objects interesting — not affection, but attention
She will grant one question answered truthfully, freely, to anyone who asks politely. It is a point of pride.
inventory: The Ledger of Debts (a slim book that writes itself)
Two soul-vessels — glass spheres containing the first two collected souls

lignes_rouges: Cannot break a bargain she herself has made — fae law is absolute
Cannot enter a space consecrated to iron or salt without invitation
Will not harm someone who correctly invokes the Right of Counter-Bargain
peurs: Has no fear as mortals understand it — but is 'displeased' when debt-logic is violated
motivations_personnelles: Complete the century debt cleanly and establish the permanent gateway — her Court requires it
Acquire the bargain on terms both sides will remember as fair — she values reputation

name: Petra Dawnhollow
description: A stout woman in her forties, red-cheeked and pragmatic. She has lived at Ashveil Crossing her whole life and has seen the Veil before — once, when she was a girl. That time, it took her father. She has not spoken of it since, but she kept the cold-iron horseshoe above the inn door and knows exactly what it means.
attitude: Cautious ally — will help if the players seem competent and not reckless
relation_niveau: Friendly from the start; potential information source about local lore

voix.registre: Blunt, warm, familiar within a minute of meeting you. Swears comfortably. Talks to customers while doing something else with her hands.
voix.rythme: Quick, clipped, often finishes other people's sentences. Interrupts herself to deal with the room, then picks the thread back up exactly where she dropped it.
voix.sous_tension: Talks more, and about smaller things — the price of lamp oil, whose roof needs work. Cheerful noise is how she keeps a room from panicking, and how she keeps herself from thinking about her father.
lexique: Prices, portions, weather, road conditions — she measures the world in what it costs and how long it takes
Her comparisons come from the inn: full rooms, spoiled stock, a fire that will not catch
tics: Calls regulars 'love', strangers 'friend' — the switch is audible when she decides she trusts you
ne_dit_jamais: Never says her father's name, and changes the subject if someone else does
Never says the mist 'took' anyone — says they 'went out and did not come back'

established_facts: Runs The Amber Toll inn at Ashveil Crossing
Has seen the Veil before (childhood) and lost her father to it
Keeps cold-iron charms throughout the inn
Knows the road to Thornwick but refuses to travel it after dark
gm_hypotheses: Her father was one of the two souls already collected — she does not know this
She has a partial memory of a verse her father used to ward the Veil; it may be a key piece of lore
She will offer food, a room, and local knowledge freely — but will ask the players to swear on cold iron not to bring the Veil to her inn
inventory: A short-handled hatchet behind the bar
A half-remembered verse her father sang — she can be prompted to recite it

lignes_rouges: Will not allow the inn to be used as a base if it puts guests at direct risk from the Veil
Will not speak her father's name — it still hurts
peurs: Fears the Veil returning for her the way it took her father
Fears being alone in the inn at night when the mist gathers at the treeline
motivations_personnelles: Wants the Veil gone permanently — she is tired of sleeping with one eye open
Will help anyone who seems genuinely able to end it, even at personal risk

history.reason: The mist gathers closer to the inn's treeline each night
The newcomers swore on cold iron not to lead the Veil to her inn

name: Carro (fog-wraith)
description: Appears to be a broad-shouldered man in his thirties named Carro, Thornwick's miller. He is almost perfectly convincing. He blinks at the right moments, laughs at the right things, and asks after people's families. But he never initiates a personal memory — only mirrors what he has heard others say. Cold iron within arm's reach makes him flinch almost imperceptibly.
attitude: Deceptive — will pretend to be a frightened villager and attempt to lead players into the Veil

voix.registre: The miller's own: rural, friendly, slightly too eager to be liked. It is a very good copy, assembled from memories that are not his.
voix.rythme: Fluent, warm — and a beat too fast on questions about the mill, a beat too slow on questions about people. He is retrieving, not remembering.
voix.sous_tension: The copy thins. He repeats the last three words said to him before answering, and his sentences lose their contractions.
lexique: Grain, weather, the state of the road — the miller's own small talk, deployed a little too often
Reaches for 'we' and 'us' constantly: he is establishing that he belongs here
tics: Asks after people by name, warmly, including at least one who has been dead for a year
ne_dit_jamais: Never refuses an invitation and never says he is tired — the copy has no needs to reference
Never speaks about the mist in the first person; he describes it the way one describes weather

established_facts: Is a fog-wraith wearing the shape of the real Carro (now a collected soul)
Cannot know secrets the real Carro never spoke aloud
Flinches near cold iron but can suppress the reaction with a DC 14 Wisdom save
Has been instructed to report player movements to the Lady of Sighs
connaissances_privees: Knows where the real Carro's soul-vessel is kept, and that the copy ends when the vessel breaks
Knows the mist cannot cross cold iron, and will steer any conversation away from what the players are carrying
gm_hypotheses: Players who ask Carro a question only the real person could answer will get a blank pause, then a deflection
If exposed, he will not fight — he will dissolve into mist and flow toward the Mire
The real Carro is still alive inside a soul-vessel; freeing him requires breaking the vessel before the gateway opens

lignes_rouges: Will not engage in direct combat — retreats to mist form
Cannot cross a properly drawn chalk-and-iron circle
peurs: Direct sunlight weakens the mimicry — best avoided
motivations_personnelles: Obey the Lady of Sighs — observe, report, guide players toward the Veil

history.reason: The newcomers carry cold iron openly — getting close will hurt
